name: Punta Nizuc
label: Punta Nizuc
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Playa Coral (El Mirador II), Punta Nizuc' (2 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from OSM R12414713 (Parque Nacional Costa Occidental de Isla Mujeres, Punta Cancún y Punta Nizuc): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Southern tip of the Hotel Zone, near the reef.

text.description:
Punta Nizuc is a point within the Parque Nacional Costa Occidental de Isla Mujeres, Punta Cancún y Punta Nizuc, in the Nizuc area of Cancún. The photo works because of its simplicity: a strip of pale sand, clear shallow water and a long horizon, with very little clutter.

The tip itself is largely behind a resort, and outside visitors may no longer be able to walk out to it. For that reason the map sends you to the public beach at Playa Coral (El Mirador II), where the shoreline and the open water around the point frame the picture. A second option is the bridge at Puente Canal Nizuc. From the bridge you look across the channel to the clear water and tropical vegetation of the Punta Nizuc area. It makes a good second photo with a different feel, because the water leads your eye into the green.

For a phone, keep the picture simple. Put the sea and sand in the frame, let the shoreline curve through it, and keep the horizon level. Do not try to reach the resort side or any private pier or pool, as those are not public. Access can change, so check local access rules before you go.
text.geographic_location: Punta Nizuc is in the Nizuc area of Cancún, near the airport road. The public beach at Playa Coral is close by.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot. Head towards the Nizuc area near the airport road and look for Playa Coral (El Mirador II) rather than the resort. Once on the public beach at Playa Coral, use the phone icon on the map as your position. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in the sand, sea and sky together. Use the default lens (1x) for a cleaner, more natural view of the shoreline. If your phone has a telephoto (2x-5x), use it to pick out the point across the water.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. From here the photo shows the Punta Nizuc shoreline and the open water on the point, with sand and sea framing the view. If you want a different angle, the bridge at Puente Canal Nizuc looks across the channel to the clear water and tropical vegetation.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the horizon on the upper or lower third line. Let the curve of the beach lead the eye towards the point. Keep a little wet sand in the foreground for interest. For a second shot, go to the bridge at Puente Canal Nizuc and photograph across the channel.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the point or the water to focus, then slide the exposure down a touch so the sky does not wash out and the water keeps its colour. Wipe the lens first, as sea spray and sunscreen leave a haze on phone cameras.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and more comfortable conditions on the beach than midday.

text.access_note: Playa Coral is a public beach, but the point itself is largely behind a resort, so check local access rules before you go.

name: Playa Delfines
label: Playa Delfines
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'El Mirador' (3 web pages); placed at our map tiles: 'Mirador playa delfines' (pois).
pin_note: Position from OSM N2611777999 (Playa Delfines): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Wide public beach with the colourful Cancún sign and open Caribbean views.

text.description:
Playa Delfines is a beach in Cancún, and its classic photograph is taken from El Mirador, the lookout platform. From the south end of the platform, the colourful CANCÚN letters sit in the foreground. Behind them are the turquoise sea and the curve of the bay. The letters frame the water nicely, and the sun is behind you, so the colours look rich and the sea looks bright.

The main viewpoint is the south end of the El Mirador platform. Start with the default lens (1x) and hold the phone level, using the gridlines, so the horizon stays straight and the bay's curve is clear. Then try the 2x zoom for a tighter, more natural-looking view of the letters and the sea. For a close, head-on shot of the letters with just the ocean behind, use the Letrero CANCÚN viewpoint instead. Come back at sunset for the sky and sea seen from the lookout.

Two practical points. The letters may be at the beach entrance or beside the lookout, so check on the day exactly where they stand before you walk. The lookout and the sign also get queues from mid-morning, and the sign is busiest around midday. Seaweed and strong surf can affect the beach from summer to autumn, and swimming currents are strong, so stay at the shoreline.
text.geographic_location: Playa Delfines is on the Caribbean coast of Cancún, and El Mirador is the lookout platform at Playa Delfines. The CANCÚN letters are at or near the lookout.
text.directions_text: From there the subject position at El Mirador is about 66 m to the east, roughly 1 minute on foot. Check on the day where the letters stand before you walk. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) to capture the letters, the sea and the curve of the bay together. Switch to 2x for a tighter, more natural-looking frame. Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) only if you want a dramatic close-up of the letters, and keep the horizon level.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject (south end of the lookout platform, sun behind the photographer). The CANCÚN letters in the foreground with the turquoise Caribbean and the curve of the bay behind them. At the south end of the El Mirador platform, with the sun behind you. From the platform the photo shows the CANCÚN letters in the foreground with the turquoise Caribbean and the curve of the bay behind them. For a closer, head-on shot of the letters, try the Letrero CANCÚN viewpoint as an alternative.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Put the letters in the foreground and let the sea fill the space behind them. Turn on the gridlines and place the horizon on the upper or lower line so it stays straight. Keep a little sky and the curve of the bay in view. At sunset, shoot from the lookout towards the water to capture the setting sun over the sea.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the sea or the letters to focus, then slide the exposure down slightly if the sky or the white sand looks too bright. Use Live Photos if people are walking through the frame, so you can choose the best moment afterwards. In the evening, use night mode only after the sun has gone, and hold the phone steady.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, roughly 7:30 to 9:30, when the light comes from the side and crowds are small. Sunset is the alternative for a colourful sky.

text.access_note: Conditions can change, so check locally before you go.

name: Playa Tortugas
label: Playa Tortugas
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Playa Tortugas' (2 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from OSM N4690582120 (Playa Tortugas): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Calm bay beach with a pier on the lagoon side.

text.description:
Playa Tortugas is a sandy beach on the calm bay side of Cancún, and it is an easy place to take relaxed, low-effort photos. The water is gentle, there are palms along the shore, and the mix of sand and a few rocky outcrops gives you more than one backdrop without walking far. That variety is what makes it worth a stop with a phone.

The spot on the map is the sand near the water at the western stretch of the beach, away from the pier. From here you can frame the waterline, the curve of the shore and the palms together, with soft evening light on the bay. It is quieter than the pier area, which is useful if you want a cleaner picture with fewer people in it.

One caution: the beach faces north, so do not count on a fiery sunset over the water. Think of it as a gentle golden-hour spot, with warm light on the sand and palms rather than a big colour show on the horizon. Conditions change from day to day, and seaweed (sargassum) can affect the shoreline on some days, so have a look at the water before you settle on a composition. The sand can also get busy, and some visitors report vendors approaching, so a polite no and a short walk west is usually enough.

If you would rather shoot from the pier, there is a separate view there; see the framing tips below.
text.geographic_location: Playa Tortugas is on the bay side of Cancún, near the pier, from which Isla Mujeres can be seen on the horizon.
text.directions_text: Search for Playa Tortugas on your map app and navigate to the beach. Once there, walk onto the sand and head to the western stretch of the beach, away from the pier. The phone icon on the map is on the sand near the water, so you can stop right at it. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the waterline, shore and palms together. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want to include more sand, a rocky outcrop in the foreground and the wide bay.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. From here the photo shows the calm bay in soft evening light, with the waterline and the palm-lined shore in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the waterline on the lower or upper third, with the palms leading along one side. Crouch a little and include some wet sand or a rock in the foreground to add depth. If you want a different view, the pier looks out to Isla Mujeres on the horizon, with colourful catamarans in front of it, best around sunrise.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the sea or sky to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down slightly so the light stays warm and the highlights on the water do not wash out. Wipe the lens first, as sea air leaves a haze on it.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Late afternoon to sunset for soft, warm light on the sand and palms. Do not expect a strong sunset colour over the water, since the beach faces north.

text.access_note: The pier is used for paid bungee and zipline activities, so check conditions locally if you plan to use it.
claims_not_in_sources: Wiping the phone lens helps when there is sea haze or spray.

name: Mercado 28
label: Mercado 28
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Avenida Yaxchilán' (1 web pages); placed at the stretch of Avenida Yaxchilán nearest the subject (our map tiles).
pin_note: Position from OSM W255581984 (Mercado 28): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Traditional downtown craft and souvenir market.

text.description:
Mercado 28 is a busy local market, and the streets around it make a good place for colourful phone photos. Many street-art murals can be found inside the market and along Avenida Yaxchilán. That avenue is the quieter option, because the market aisles can get crowded. This is a short walk from the market, so you can photograph the painted walls first and then go in for a look around.

The murals are the main subject, and a wall is easy to photograph because it holds still and you can step back from it. Walk the stretch slowly and keep an eye out for painted walls. I can't say exactly where each mural is, so check on the day. If you want the market itself, its entrance and arch make a good frame for a wider shot. Take a few steps back so the whole entrance fits. Inside, ask vendors before taking close-up photos of them or their goods. Be careful about which building you navigate to, as another, unrelated building with a similar name can cause confusion. Use the Xel-Há address, Supermanzana 28, Manzana 13.
text.geographic_location: Mercado 28 is in the Xel-Há area of Cancún, at Supermanzana 28, Manzana 13.
text.directions_text: No public transport stops are listed for this spot, so navigate using the address Supermanzana 28, Manzana 13 (Xel-Há) for the market. Walk east from the market to reach it, or head west from it to reach the market. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Use the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit a long painted wall into one frame when you cannot step back far. Switch to the default lens (1x) for straight-on shots of a single mural, and use telephoto (2x or more) for details such as faces or lettering.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Avenida Yaxchilán (stretch between Avenida Xcaret and Avenida Sunyaxchen, near the market). Street-art murals on the walls of the street, with the market a short walk away for context. On the stretch between Avenida Xcaret and Avenida Sunyaxchen, near the market. From there you are looking at the street-art murals on the walls, with the market a short walk away. Walk the stretch slowly and photograph the walls you find.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line the edge of a wall up with a vertical line so the mural does not lean. Keep the phone level to avoid stretched edges. For a different shot, go to the market entrance and step back so the entrance and its arch fit in the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the mural to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little if the sky or a bright wall washes out the colours. Take a few frames of each wall, since people and vehicles pass through.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Go during the day, when the market is open, and avoid the busiest times if you want clear shots of the street. Check the market's current opening hours before you go.

text.access_note: The avenue is a public street, but the market is a working commercial space, so check its current opening hours before you go.

name: Playa Gaviota Azul
label: Playa Gaviota Azul
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Plaza Forum' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Plaza Forum Cancun' (way/200451675): middle (170 m across); moved 30 m off buildings.
pin_note: Position from OSM N4126837609 (Playa Gaviota Azul): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Popular beach on the Hotel Zone's north stretch.

text.description: Playa Gaviota Azul is a city beach in Cancún, and its main draw for photos is colour: turquoise water, a pale shoreline and, as the name suggests, gulls. The most distinctive picture here is from above rather than on the sand. From the upper balcony of Plaza Forum you look down onto the beach, so the gulls, the strip of sand and the water stack neatly into layers. A raised view like this is easy for a phone to handle, because the water fills much of the frame and the colours do the work. If you want the more traditional beach shot, go down to the sand afterwards. The shoreline there is framed by palm trees, which makes a pleasant tropical backdrop for portraits of friends and family. Conditions change from day to day. The beach is exposed, seaweed (sargassum) can build up on some days, and a breakwater calms the northern end of the beach. If the water near you looks cloudy or the shore is covered in weed, shoot from the balcony, where the line of the shore matters more than the detail. Some guides also recommend the beach at sunset, so it is worth planning a second visit if your first is in the middle of the day. Keep the horizon level using your gridlines, and keep any people or birds away from the very edge of the frame.
text.geographic_location: Playa Gaviota Azul is a beach in Cancún, close to the Plaza Forum shopping centre, which looks out over it.
text.directions_text: Head for Plaza Forum in Cancún. The beach (the subject) is about 109 m to the east. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the view down onto the beach. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in more of the shoreline, or to 2x-3x telephoto to pick out the gulls and a patch of turquoise water.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand at Plaza Forum (upper balcony overlooking the beach). A raised view down onto the beach and the gulls and turquoise water along the shoreline. The recommended view is from the upper balcony overlooking the beach, though it is worth checking balcony access on the day. From there you look down onto the beach, with the gulls and the turquoise water along the shoreline spread out below you. The beach itself lies to the east.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the shoreline along one of the lower lines, so the water and sand fill the frame. Keep the balcony rail out of the shot by holding the phone just above it. For an alternative, walk down to Playa Gaviota Azul itself and frame the turquoise shoreline with palm trees for beach portraits.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the water to focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the turquoise stays rich and the sand does not turn white. Try a Live Photo when gulls are flying, then choose the best frame afterwards. Use portrait mode only for people on the sand.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Some guides recommend sunset, so that is a good time to try. Otherwise, go on a day when the water looks clear, as seaweed can build up on this exposed beach.

text.access_note: Please check on the day whether visitors can use the Plaza Forum balcony, or look at the official site before you go.

name: Kukulcan Plaza
label: Kukulcan Plaza
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Kukulcan Plaza' (3 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from OSM N6401644286 (R1-Rehoyada - Plaza Kukulcan): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Large shopping mall in the middle of the Hotel Zone.

text.description:
Kukulcan Plaza is a shopping mall on Boulevard Kukulcán, and the best photo inside it is looking straight up. The central atrium is topped by a stained-glass dome with a Mayan-inspired pattern, and from underneath the colours and geometry fill the frame. A fountain in the lobby close by gives you something to include at the bottom of the picture if you want a sense of the space around you.

It works well on a phone because the subject is large, bright and graphic, and you don't need to be far away. Stand right under the dome and tilt the phone upwards. The ultra-wide lens (0.5x) fits in the whole dome and some of the atrium's edges. The default lens (1x) suits a tighter shot of the pattern.

Guides point to this atrium as the main photo subject indoors, and they note that personal photography is allowed there. It is a working shopping centre, so be considerate: step to the side of walkways, don't block shoppers while you line up the shot, and avoid holding up other people. The atrium is a bright, enclosed space, so check the screen for glare from the glass and adjust if the dome looks washed out. Allow a few minutes for a handful of different angles. Straight up, slightly off-centre, and one with the fountain included will give you a good choice to pick from later.
text.geographic_location: Kukulcan Plaza is a shopping mall on Boulevard Kukulcán in Cancún. The photo spot is inside, in the central atrium.
text.directions_text: No station or tram stop is listed for this spot, so look up the mall's address on Boulevard Kukulcán in a maps app and navigate from there. Once inside, walk to the central atrium and stand under the stained-glass dome. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide lens (0.5x) to fit the whole dome in from below. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a closer shot of the pattern.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. From here the photo shows the dome's Mayan-inspired pattern from below, with the lobby fountain nearby.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Point the phone upwards and turn on gridlines to keep the dome centred, or place it slightly off-centre for a more relaxed picture. For a second shot, step back and include the fountain at the bottom of the frame. Keep the phone level with the dome to avoid the edges leaning inwards.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the glass to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the colours stay rich and the bright dome doesn't turn pale.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Choose a time when the atrium is not too busy so you can stand and frame the shot without blocking people. Check the official site for opening times before you go.

text.access_note: This is an indoor shopping mall where personal photography is allowed in the atrium; check the official site before you go for opening times and any rules.

notes: Popular public beach in the Hotel Zone.

text.description: Playa Chac Mool is a Caribbean beach on Cancún's Hotel Zone coast, and the best view of it is from the rocky outcrop at its northern end. From that higher ground you look back along the shoreline, with dark rocks and surf close to you and the long curve of the beach behind. That gives a phone photo plenty of depth: texture in the foreground, then water and sand leading away. Guides to the beach single this outcrop out as a strong vantage point for a panoramic coastline view. They also say the rocky sections at either end make striking contrast shots against the ocean, and that it is a quieter alternative to the sandy centre of the beach. If you would rather stay on the sand, the other classic frame has turquoise water and white sand in the foreground and the Hotel Zone skyline on the opposite side of the picture. The sea here can be rough, and seaweed (sargassum) conditions change from day to day, so the water may not look the same as in pictures you have seen. It is sensible to check the sea and sargassum conditions before you go. One reviewer who visited on a Sunday found few people, so a weekday morning may be quieter still. Sunset is suggested as a time for colourful skies over the water. Take care on the wet rocks and keep one hand free for your phone.
text.geographic_location: Playa Chac Mool is on the Hotel Zone coast of Cancún, reached from Blvd. Kukulcán at km 10, opposite Señor Frogs.
text.directions_text: No station or stop is listed for this spot. The beach access is on Blvd. Kukulcán in the Hotel Zone at km 10, opposite Señor Frogs. There is no parking at the beach access, so plan how you will arrive. Walk down to the sand and turn to the rocky end at the northern end of the beach. The phone icon on the map is on that rocky outcrop. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to take in the rocks, surf and the sweep of coastline in one frame. Switch to the default lens (1x) for a calmer, less stretched view of the water. If your phone has a telephoto (2x-5x), use it to pick out waves breaking on the rocks.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. From here the beach and coastline are seen from higher ground, with the rocks and surf in front of you and the shoreline sweeping away behind. If the rocks feel slippery or the surf is high, take the photo from the sand instead, with the turquoise water in the foreground and the Hotel Zone skyline on the other side of the frame.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the rocks in the lower third, with the line of the beach running diagonally into the picture. Keep the horizon level. For a wider view, try a slow panorama along the coast, holding the phone steady and upright.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the sea or sand to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky and the white foam keep their detail. Try a Live Photo to catch the movement of the surf, and wipe the lens first, as sea spray leaves marks.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunset is suggested for colourful skies over the water. One reviewer who visited on a Sunday found few people, so a weekday morning may be quieter.

text.access_note: Beach access is from Blvd. Kukulcán at km 10, opposite Señor Frogs, with no parking; sea and seaweed conditions vary, so check local conditions before you go.

label: Punta Cancún
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Faro Punta Cancún' (5 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).

notes: Headland at the Hotel Zone's bend with beach views of both sides.

text.description: Punta Cancún is the northern tip of the hotel zone, where the land bends round and the coast changes character. The focus here is Faro Punta Cancún, a red-and-white lighthouse on a rocky point, at Blvd. Kukulcán km 9, behind the Hyatt Ziva. On one side is the open Caribbean. On the other, the lagoon and the hotel-zone coastline stretch back behind it. Guides call it the classic photo subject of this area, and the sea views are wide. On a clear day Isla Mujeres shows up in the distance, which gives you a good second layer in the frame. The red and white of the tower stands out well against blue water and sky, so even a quick snap looks tidy. Reviewers say it works well for a short photo stop rather than a long visit. The rocks are sharp and the wind can be strong, so wear proper shoes and hold your phone firmly with both hands. Try a wide shot that includes the rocks in the foreground, then a closer one that fills the frame with the tower. Access is the one thing to plan for. The lighthouse sits on Hyatt Ziva property, and you reach it by walking over the rocky shoreline from the public beach at Playa Caracol or through the hotel grounds. Guards sometimes restrict passage, so it is not guaranteed.
text.geographic_location: At the northern tip of the hotel zone (Zona Hotelera) in Cancún, on Blvd. Kukulcán at km 9, behind the Hyatt Ziva and not far from the public beach at Playa Caracol.
text.directions_text: Follow Blvd. Kukulcán to km 9, at the northern tip of the hotel zone. The lighthouse is behind the Hyatt Ziva. From the public beach at Playa Caracol you can walk over the rocky shoreline towards it, but wear shoes. Guards sometimes restrict passage, so have a plan B. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) to fit the lighthouse, the rocks and the open sea in one frame. The default lens (1x) is better for a cleaner shot of the tower alone. If your phone has a telephoto (2x-5x), use it to pick out Isla Mujeres in the distance or to crop in on the lighthouse.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Kukulcán km 9, behind the Hyatt Ziva. Frame the red-and-white tower from the nearby rocks, with the Caribbean on one side and the lagoon and hotel-zone coastline behind it.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and put the lighthouse on one of the vertical lines, with the sea filling the other two-thirds. Keep a few rocks in the foreground for depth. For a second shot, aim out to sea and let Isla Mujeres sit on the horizon, if it is visible.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the lighthouse to focus, then slide the exposure down a little so the white paint keeps its detail against the bright sky. Hold the phone with both hands in the wind, and wipe the lens if it gets salty spray.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Sunrise or the golden hour before sunset, which is when guides describe the best light here.

text.access_note: The lighthouse is on Hyatt Ziva property, reached over the rocky shoreline from Playa Caracol or through the hotel grounds; guards sometimes restrict passage, so have a plan B.
claims_not_in_sources: Sea spray and salt can get onto a phone lens near the water, so wiping it helps.
Lowering the exposure slider helps keep detail in white surfaces against a bright sky.

camera_source: No separate stand-here point: photographed at the spot itself (indoors, from its top, or right in front of it); drawn as the split pin.
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q14825940: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Modern museum next to the San Miguelito ruins.

text.description: The Museo Maya de Cancún is an archaeology museum in the Hotel Zone, and it makes a calm change from the beach. It opened on 2 November 2012, timed to coincide with the end of the Mayan Long Count calendar that December. The building was designed by Alberto García Lascurain and holds more than 350 artefacts from Mayan communities across the Yucatán Peninsula. The building covers about 55,000 square feet on a 20-acre complex. Around it are some 40 Mayan structures, including a 26-foot pyramid at the San Miguelito archaeological site. That mix of modern museum architecture and old stonework is what makes it worth a few photos. Good frames include the clean lines of the museum building, with green planting around it, and the contrast between the new building and the ancient structures nearby. From the phone icon on the map you are right at the subject, so you can try the building as a whole and then move closer for details. Step back where the layout allows, keep the phone level so the walls don't lean, and take a few frames from different heights. If you also visit the ruins area, keep an eye on the paths and any signs about where you may walk or photograph.
text.geographic_location: In the Hotel Zone (Zona Hotelera) of Cancún, Quintana Roo. The museum shares its complex with the San Miguelito archaeological site.
text.directions_text: No public transport stops are listed near the Museo Maya de Cancún, so check the official site before you go for the best way to arrive and for entrance details. The phone icon on the map is at the museum itself, so once you arrive there is no further walk to the spot. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the building as you see it. Switch to the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you cannot step back far enough to fit the whole front in. Use the telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for stonework, carvings and the pyramid's details.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Photograph the building from wherever you have a clear view, and move a few steps left or right until the lines look balanced.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and line up the edges of the building with them so the walls stay straight. Include a little foreground, such as planting or a path, to give a sense of scale. For the ancient structures, frame a single pyramid or wall against the sky, then take a second shot with the museum building in view to show the contrast.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the brightest wall to focus, then slide the exposure slider down a touch so the sky keeps its colour and the stonework isn't washed out. Ultra-wide shots can stretch the corners, so keep people and important details away from the edges.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Morning or late afternoon usually gives softer light and fewer harsh shadows on the building. In the middle of the day the light is strong, so use the exposure slider to avoid washed-out walls.

text.access_note: The museum and the archaeological site may be ticketed with set visiting times and rules, so check the official site before you go.

name: Playa Caracol
label: Playa Caracol
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Playa Caracol' (2 web pages); placed at OpenStreetMap 'Playa Caracol' (way/1154140709): edge nearest the subject (782 m across); moved 5 m off water.
pin_note: Position from OSM N4782242364 (Playa Caracol): kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Beach at the bend of the Hotel Zone, near Punta Cancún.

text.description:
Playa Caracol is a small white-sand beach in Cancún's hotel strip, with the Isla Mujeres ferry pier reaching out over turquoise water. That pier is what makes the pictures work. Its long line leads the eye out to sea, and the water gives you plenty of colour without any editing.

For something different from the usual open-beach view, go under the pier on the beach side. From there you get a framed shot of the pier's length and the water beneath it. The sections of sea under the pier can be cleaner and less crowded than the open sand, which helps if seaweed (sargassum) has washed up. Seaweed comes and goes, so check how the beach looks on the day.

If you would rather have the classic view, step back onto the sand and shoot the pier extending into the water behind the beach.

Most of the shoreline here is backed by hotels, so public access is limited to a few marked entry points. Beach chairs and umbrellas are rented from a government booth. Check the exact entrance on the map before you set off.

On your phone, keep the lens clean, hold the camera low for the pier shot, and use the gridlines to keep the pier straight. Take one wide frame and one tighter frame so you have both the setting and the detail.
text.geographic_location: Playa Caracol is on the Cancún hotel strip, on the seafront side, with hotels behind the beach. Guides place it around the Mocambo Square/Aloft area and the Super Chedraui side.
text.directions_text: No Underground, tram or station stops are listed nearby, so use the map to reach the Mocambo Square/Aloft area or the Super Chedraui side of the hotel strip. Look for the sign on the road that marks a public beach entry point, and check the exact entrance on the map. The Navigate buttons below take you to the subject.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the ultra-wide (0.5x) if you go under the pier, so the pier's length and the water both fit in the frame. Use the default lens (1x) for the classic beach-and-pier view. If your phone has a telephoto (2x-5x), use it to pick out the far end of the pier without walking closer.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand on Playa Caracol (under the pier, on the beach side). A framed shot of the long pier and the water beneath it, with cleaner sections of sea that can be less crowded than the open beach. Once you are there, you can try going under the pier on the beach side as a separate option, to frame the long pier and the water beneath it. The cleaner stretches of sea under the pier can be less crowded than the open beach.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Use the pier's line as a leading line and turn on gridlines so the uprights stay level. Keep the sea in the lower part of the frame and leave some sky above. For the other classic view, walk out onto the open sand and shoot the pier extending into the turquoise water behind the small white beach.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap on the water to set focus, then drag the exposure slider down a little so the sky and the sea keep their colour. Try a Live Photo for the moving water and wipe the lens first, as sea spray leaves marks.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Go when the beach is quietest, and check on the day whether seaweed has washed up, as that changes the water and the shots.

text.access_note: The beach is mostly backed by hotels, so public access is limited to a few marked entry points; check the exact entrance on the map before you go.

name: El Rey Archaeological Zone
label: El Rey ruins
camera_source: Researched viewpoint 'Zona Arqueológica El Rey' (3 web pages); placed at at the subject (split pin).
pin_note: Position from Wikidata Q1324550: kept: no OpenStreetMap object carries this Wikidata ID.
notes: Small Maya site in the Hotel Zone, home to many iguanas.

text.description: El Rey is a small Maya site tucked among the hotels of Cancún, and that contrast is what makes it fun to photograph. Low stone platforms, a stepped pyramid and palms sit in the foreground, and with the right angle the Hotel Zone skyline shows up behind them. The site has 47 structures, and the ones you see today date from roughly 1300 to 1500 AD, when El Rey was a port on the Caribbean coast. Its name, 'the king', comes from a sculpture that looked like a monarch. The head is now in the Archaeological Museum of Cancún. For the strongest picture, start in the main plaza and use the stepped pyramid as your anchor, with the palms and low platforms around it. A second option is a wide view across the lagoon towards the Hotel Zone, with the ruins in the foreground. A third is a quieter view over the stonework framed by jungle brush, which keeps other visitors out of the shot. Iguanas are common here and may sit right where you want to stand, so give them space and photograph them as a bonus. Go early if you can: the light is softer and tour groups have not yet arrived. Check the official site before you go for current opening times and entry rules.
text.geographic_location: El Rey is in the Hotel Zone, on the island part of Cancún that is joined to the mainland by two bridges, a short way from the city centre. It sits among the resort hotels and close to the lagoon.
text.directions_text: The site is in the Hotel Zone; ask for the El Rey archaeological zone or navigate to it on a map. Once inside, walk to the main plaza and the stepped pyramid, which is where the phone icon on the map sits. The phone icon on the map is at the subject itself. The Navigate buttons below take you straight there.

shooting_on_your_phone.phone_lens: Start with the default lens (1x) for the pyramid, the palms and the platforms together. Switch to ultra-wide (0.5x) if you want the whole plaza in one frame. Use telephoto (2x-5x, depending on your phone) for stonework details, or to photograph iguanas from a polite distance.
shooting_on_your_phone.where_to_stand: Stand right at the subject: the phone icon on the map marks the spot. Stand in the main plaza of Zona Arqueológica El Rey, by the small stepped pyramid and its platform near the centre of the largest plaza.
shooting_on_your_phone.how_to_frame: Turn on gridlines and place the pyramid on one of the lines, with palms at the edges to frame it. Crouch a little so the platforms lead the eye towards the steps. For a different view, try the wide outlook over the lagoon towards the Hotel Zone with the ruins in front, or the quieter angle over the ruins framed by jungle brush.
shooting_on_your_phone.phone_settings_tip: Tap the pyramid to focus, then slide the exposure down slightly so the sky keeps its colour and the stone stays warm. Panorama mode suits the lagoon view. Leave the flash off, as it may be discouraged in some areas and does nothing for distant stone.
shooting_on_your_phone.best_time: Early morning, when the light is softest and tour groups have not arrived. Check the official site for opening times, as the gates may not open at sunrise.

text.access_note: This is a fenced archaeological site where an entry fee applies, so check the official site before you go for current hours and rules.
claims_not_in_sources: Climbing on the ruins is normally not permitted, so photograph the pyramid from the plaza and the marked paths.
The ultra-wide lens (0.5x) helps fit a whole plaza into the frame when space is tight.
